chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abi Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
He said to me: 'If you were to perform wudu (ablution) and make the wiping of the feet into washing, then inwardly hold that this is among what is obligatory, that would not be a wudu (ablution).'
Then he said: 'Begin with wiping over the feet; then if it occurs to you to wash, and you wash them, then wipe afterward so that the last of that may be the obligatory act.'

And what he mentioned after that from his statement: if a person wishes to wash his feet to remove harm from them, clean them, or cool them, then let him do that before the wudu (ablution); then let him perform wudu (ablution) after it, and conclude his wudu (ablution) with wiping his feet, so that he may be complying with the command of Allah the Exalted regarding the order of wudu (ablution).

So the preceding report indicates this, because he said: begin with wiping over the feet; then if it occurs to you to wash, and you wash them—meaning, if you want to clean them—then wipe afterward so that the last of that may be the obligatory act.

key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the two feet, the limbs discussed in the ruling of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْمَفْرُوضِ: that which is obligatory in the divine law
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَرْتِيبِ: the prescribed order or sequence of acts in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.تَنْظِيفِهِمَا: cleaning them; a permitted non-ritual reason for washing the feet
key_terms.غَسْلًا: washing; here contrasted with the obligatory wiping of the feet
key_terms.مَسْحَ: wiping; the prescribed act to be performed over the feet in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Does washing the feet instead of wiping them count as valid wudu (ablution) in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that in wudu (ablution), the feet are to be wiped as the obligatory act, and treating their washing as the obligation invalidates the wudu (ablution). If one washes the feet for cleaning or cooling, that should be done before wudu (ablution), and the wudu (ablution) must conclude with wiping the feet.
